summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Q1 (system NPL ratio, capital adequacy, sectoral credit concentration), Q2 (private credit to productive sectors vs real estate and trade) and Q3 (account-ownership and borrowing gaps by province and gender) are pending. Primary leads: NRB Financial Stability Report Issue 17 (FY2024/25) and FY2022/23 FSR, NRB Bank Supervision Department release for mid-January 2026 (surfaced by this session's single search), NRB CME releases (sectoral credit tables), Monetary Policy FY2025/26 and mid-term review (productive-sector lending requirements and macroprudential limits), IMF 2026 Article IV/seventh ECF review (financial-sector section, loan-portfolio review) and prior sixth review, World Bank Financial Sector Stability DPC2 and NDU April 2026; for inclusion, Global Findex, WDI account-ownership codes, IMF FAS and NRB province-level access statistics (the last three are general-knowledge URLs, unverified). Method: banking health table by institution class and FY; credit taxonomy mapping NRB sector codes into productive / real estate / trade / consumption / other; inclusion gaps from Findex (gender, national) and NRB supply-side data (province), noting Findex lacks province detail. No numbers reported; secondary news items seen in the search were not used.

findings.claim: Productive-credit taxonomy (working definition): productive = agriculture, forestry, fisheries; mining; manufacturing; construction excluding residential real estate; electricity, gas and water; tourism (hotels and restaurants); transport and communications. Real estate = residential and commercial real estate lending, land and housing development, home loans. Trade = wholesale and retail. Consumption and other = consumable loans, margin/share loans, other services. To be reconciled with NRB sector codes and NRB's own productive-sector definition.
findings.note: Definition only; drives estimate construction in r2.

findings.claim: Headline NPL ratios are sensitive to classification forbearance and restructuring relief; reported NPL is treated as a lower bound on problem assets unless the portfolio review indicates otherwise.
findings.note: Hypothesis to be tested against IMF/NRB review documents; not a finding.

data_gaps: No NRB, IMF, WB or Findex file downloaded in r1; all values pending retrieval in r2.
Exact URL of NRB 'Banking and Financial Statistics' monthly/quarterly publication files (BSD) not confirmed beyond the mid-January 2026 page.

Findex does not report province-level results for Nepal; province gaps rely on NRB supply-side counts and Census population; gender-by-province borrowing may be unavailable except from NLSS IV microdata.
Loan-portfolio / asset-quality review results under the IMF ECF may be partly confidential; public scope unknown.
NRB sector codes changed over time; a concordance is required for a consistent FY2015/16-latest series.
Several leads (Findex, WDI financial codes, IMF FSI/FAS, NRB directives and publications archive, NSO) are from general knowledge and marked unverified.

assumptions.text: Class A commercial banks dominate system assets; the banking health table reports Class A, B, C separately and a system aggregate weighted by loans; weights to be computed from retrieved data, not assumed.
Productive-credit taxonomy as stated in findings; any change is logged as a methodological revision.
FY-end (mid-July) stocks are the primary period; mid-month intra-year points are labelled with Nepali and Gregorian dates.

challenges.text: Banking capacity to fund a high-investment path depends on asset quality and capital; until NPL/CAR and portfolio-review results are retrieved, scenario credit-growth assumptions for STR-A..E should be flagged as unverified.

Register watch item: NPL ratio NRB (FY, national classification) vs IMF FSI/WDI FB.AST.NPER.ZS (possibly CY, FSI methodology) - likely definitional/vintage; and CAR (NRB Basel) vs WDI capital-to-assets (different concept, not a conflict).
Correspondent-banking exposure (CPMI) and NRB FSR Issue 17 overlap; please share any FSR table references on foreign-currency exposures so 03B does not duplicate extraction.

uncertainty: High. No value retrieved. NPL measurement depends on classification rules and forbearance; sector codes change over time; province and gender inclusion gaps rely on sparse survey waves (Findex) and supply-side counts that do not identify individuals. Productive-credit shares depend on the taxonomy chosen.

banking_health_table.question: What are the system NPL ratio, capital adequacy and sectoral credit concentration?
banking_health_table.rows_planned: FY2015/16-latest FY-end plus latest mid-month, Class A/B/C and system
banking_health_table.method: Extract from NRB FSR and BSD statistics; cross-check against IMF FSI and staff report tables; compute HHI across NRB sector codes (estimate); document loan-classification and capital-framework changes by date.

credit_allocation_table.question: How much private credit flows to productive sectors versus real estate and trade?
credit_allocation_table.unit: NPR_current_mn and percent of total private credit
credit_allocation_table.method: Map NRB sector-wise credit codes to categories (03B-A2); build FY-end series FY2015/16-latest; compare with NRB productive-sector definition and directed-lending requirements; express private credit as percent of NSO nominal GDP; note that collateral-based lending to 'productive' borrowers may finance real estate (qualitative caveat).

inclusion_gaps.question: What is the account-ownership and borrowing gap by province and gender?

dimensions.gender: Findex (national, survey years) and FAS where sex-disaggregated
dimensions.province: NRB branch/account counts per adult with Census 2021 population; NLSS IV household borrowing sources

inclusion_gaps.method: Gender gap = male minus female in percentage points (Findex); province gap = province value minus national, supply-side; flag that deposit-account counts exceed individuals (multiple accounts) so they are not ownership rates.
